title: Primal-Spectral Generative Modeling: Fast Analytical Generation via Pseudoinverse Lévy Inversion
claim: Local, isotropic smoothing of samples leaves weak gradients away from data; a global spectral representation gives valid gradients everywhere.
layout: 2 panels side by side, 3D surfaces, shared blue query-point marker
description: Two 3D surface plots compare gradient landscapes over an X–Y plane for a noisy point x_t, marked by a blue cross. Panel (a), titled 'Primal Approach: Local & Isotropic Smoothing', shows three sharp orange peaks with dark red sample dots on top. The flat, pale floor between the peaks is labeled in blue 'Weak Gradient (Implicit Global Geometry)'. Panel (b), titled 'Spectral Approach: Global Representation', shows a smooth, broad viridis-colored surface with three gentle bumps. Green dots mark the samples, and the surface is continuous at the blue cross. A red label reads 'Valid Gradient (Phase Consistency)'. Large bold titles sit on top. The eye goes first to the tall orange peaks, then to the smooth colorful surface on the right. Axes run from -4 to 4, and the z-axis scales differ between panels.
caption: Gradient landscape comparison for noisy data xt
abstract: A probability distribution $\mathbb{P}$ is a measure on a $\sigma$-algebra, assigning mass to sets rather than points, which poses a challenge for the training of neural networks that often struggle to reconstruct the global topology of continuous manifolds from sparse samples. We mitigate this issue by transforming $\mathbb{P}$ into a continuous function via spectral methods, providing theoretical guarantees for the convergence of the learned distribution to the true distribution. Specifically, we introduce a network, PriSpecNet, with a single-function evaluation (1-NFE) Pseudoinverse L\'evy Inversion (PiLI) solver that regards generation as a fast analytical problem, eliminating the need for iterative numerical integration while maintaining full compatibility with the stochastic interpolants. We test our PriSpecNet in two applications: for time series, it unifies generation and forecasting, outperforming state-of-the-art (SOTA) baselines with Context-FID reductions of 50.0\%, 41.5\%, 80.6\%, and 63.1\% on Sines, Solar, ETTh, and Stock benchmarks, respectively, also decreasing forecasting MSE by 29.8\% on Solar and 23.8\% on Stock. For ImageNet $256 \times 256$, 1-NFE PiLI achieves a competitive FID of **1.66** using only **26** Gflops, representing a **170$\times$** reduction in total Gflops compared to the 4,436 Gflops required by the 25-NFE DPM-Solver++.
